title: About 6 months in and just over 1000 commits, I'm preparing to launch my first game
author: Enefium
selftext:
Reveria is a turn-based narrative-driven adventure game, coming to Steam on November 2nd with a demo out already for Steam Next Fest.

I started working on Reveria about 6 months ago, using Claude Code for the actual gameplay and Gemini for the artwork. I bought some assets from [itch.io](http://itch.io) as well (for the ability, equipment, potions, etc. icons, and spell effects mostly).

I use Claude in the command line, because I find it easier to have multiple panels open in parallel that way. Especially in early development, this helped me to speed up building the core components of the game (the different panels, the core combat loop, dungeon navigation, etc.).

Something that helped me a lot is building "generators" for different parts of my game. This is essentially code that allows me to write down new content (for example a new dungeon) in a compact and easy to read/write format that can then be parsed by the generator to create the actual in-game code. For me, this was a nice method of keeping hand-authored content in my game, while still leveraging the capability of Claude to actually implement it. And it's repeatable, because the generator is actual code that can be run for any number of new pieces of content.

Keeping art consistently in the same style has been a challenge and it's still the most tedious part of development. I basically upload examples of existing art (characters, encounter maps, towns, etc.) to Gemini and ask for something new "in the same art style as the attached image(s)".

Happy to hear what you all think and any feedback on either the game or the development process is very welcome!

Much love,

Nicholas
